mention.lead_sentence: The figures presented on the following pages summarize the data that were collected for each of the four

items.note: Grouped vertical bars over twelve simulation types - Fast/Slow x Computer / Accident Prone / Normal x Heavy/Light - with five lane-count series in a darkening grey ramp, keyed OUTSIDE the frame at the right as 'two lanes' to 'six lanes'. The in-image title is 'AVERAGE FLOW RATES OF RIGHT HAND RULE', with 'Average Cars/unit of time' up the y axis to 4 and 'Simulation Type' under the rotated x labels. Complete frame, horizontal gridlines at every tick, no vertical gridlines, no data labels. The tick label 'Fast-Accident Proine-Light' is the paper's typo. No group draws all five series, so the legend promises more bars than any group shows [geometry.legend].

items.note: The accident twin of the same simulation grid: 'RIGHT HAND RULE AVERAGE ACCIDENTS' over the same twelve types, y 'Average Number of Accidents' 0 to 2000 by 200, same five-series grey legend outside right, complete frame and horizontal gridlines. Two of the twelve groups carry all the bars - Fast-Accident Prone-Heavy reaching 1800 and Slow-Accident Prone-Heavy about 1500 - and the rest are near-empty, which is the shape the accident counts really have [geometry.printed_numbers].

Two bars reach 3.5 and 3.3 with no headroom label. Twelve simulation types on the x axis, all legible, this time spelled 'Fast-Accident Prone-Light' correctly, so the typo on p8 is not systematic.

Ten of the twelve simulation types show no bars at all, only Fast-Accident Prone-Heavy (four bars) and Slow-Accident Prone-Heavy (two) carry any, and y runs 0 to 2500 by 500 [geometry.legend].

note: Eight measured regions over four of seventeen pages, and every one of them an exhibit: eight grouped bar charts over twelve simulation types, one flow chart and one accident chart for each of the four rule systems, on pages 8 to 11. Families: 8 `bar`, uniform, no tables, no exclusions, nothing unresolved and no declared gaps. Not one chart carries a figure number - the titles are drawn inside the artwork in small caps and the text layer prints no caption line anywhere - so all eight rows record an empty caption with `caption_source` none, and the only prose pointers are the section-4.2 lead sentence and one positional reference on p12. Faults worth carrying downstream: the flow charts use three different y scales (0-4, 0-4, 0-3.5), the p9 accident legend lists 'three lanes' twice and never 'four lanes', no group on the p8 or p9 flow plates draws all five series the legend promises, only the p11 accident plate labels its data, and the p8 x labels print 'Fast-Accident Proine-Light'.
rules: No exhibit in this paper is numbered. Not one of the eight charts has a printed caption line in the text layer, and no prose sentence cites a figure by number: the only pointer is the section-4.2 lead 'The figures presented on the following pages summarize the data that were collected for each of the four', plus one structural reference on p12. All eight rows therefore record an empty caption, `caption_source` none and numbering none [caption.numbering].

The chart titles are drawn INSIDE the artwork - 'AVERAGE FLOW RATES OF RIGHT HAND RULE' and the like - in small caps, so they are quoted in the row notes and are not mistaken for captions; the caption fields stay empty rather than carrying an in-image title as if it were a caption [caption.verbatim].

All eight charts are one construction: grouped vertical bars, twelve simulation-type groups, a grey-to-black ramp of lane-count series keyed outside the frame at the right, a complete frame, horizontal gridlines at every tick and rotated text labels on the x axis with no numeric x scale [geometry.family].

Four of the eight are flow charts and four are accident charts, and the flow charts do not share a y scale: 0 to 4 on p8, 0 to 4 on p9 and 0 to 3.5 on p10, so only the accident charts (all 0 to 2000, 2500, 2500 and 3000) are even roughly comparable [geometry.printed_numbers].

The accident plates are mostly empty by nature: accidents only appear in the two accident-prone-heavy groups, so ten of the twelve x slots carry no bar on most accident charts. An empty group is not a missing series and is not counted as an exclusion [geometry.legend].

Two legends are defective. The p9 accident chart lists five swatches of which two both read 'three lanes' with no 'four lanes' entry, and on the p8 and p9 flow charts no group draws all five series the legend promises; both are recorded as printed [geometry.legend].

Exactly one plate writes values onto its data - the p11 accident chart, with 211.3, 98.8, 66.2, 97.3, 30.6, 102 and 86.1 beside the small bars and nothing beside the two tall ones - so `data_labels` is true on that row alone [geometry.data_labels].

The eight pointers are deictic. Seven rows quote the section-4.2 lead sentence one to four pages before their plate, and the p11 accident chart quotes the p12 sentence 'This can be seen in the second figure of Section 4.2.4', which points back a page and by position rather than by number, so it carries `lead_pages` -1 [mention.lead_pages].

Section paths come from the four rule headings the paper prints - 4.2.1 Right Hand Rule, 4.2.2 No Rules, 4.2.3 No Lane Changes, 4.2.4 Middle Lane Rule - under 4.2 Figures, so each plate sits on the heading that names the rule it charts instead of on a flattened 4.2 path [place.section_path].
